privacy.heading: Before you start
privacy.intro: Applai runs entirely in your browser. There is no server, no account and no sign-in. Four things you should know before you start.

provider.title: Your text goes to the AI provider you choose.
provider.body: Your cover letter and the job ad are sent from your browser straight to Google, OpenAI or Anthropic, depending on which one you pick. Without that step there are no suggestions. Applai replaces name, address, date of birth, phone number and email address with placeholders beforehand; the rest of the text goes as it is.

training.title: On the free Gemini tier, Google uses your text for training.
training.body: Google uses input and output from the free tier to develop its products and models, and people at Google may read it while doing so. For the paid tier Google states the opposite; OpenAI and Anthropic state the same for their APIs.

draft.title: A working copy stays in your browser.
draft.body: So that nothing is lost, Applai keeps your work in progress in your browser's database, along with the application list and your settings. None of it leaves the device. Drafts are deleted after export, and after seven days at the latest.

delete.title: “Delete all data” is available at any time.
delete.body: One button in the settings removes the application list, the drafts, the settings and the stored API key in one go. After that nothing of Applai is left on this device.

key.heading: Set up your API key
key.intro: Applai has no account and no server of its own. The AI requests run through your own account with one of the three providers. The key for that stays encrypted in your browser.
key.replaceHint: This browser already holds a key. Saving replaces it without a further prompt. OpenAI and Anthropic show a key only once, so a replaced one cannot be retrieved there.
key.guideHeading: How to get a key from {{provider}}
key.legacyGeminiKey: Already have a key that starts with “AIza”? Google stops accepting those keys in September 2026. Create a new one in Google AI Studio in good time; the free tier stays the same.

gemini.step1: Sign in to Google AI Studio with a Google account.
gemini.step2: Open “Get API key” and create a new key.
gemini.step3: Copy the key. New keys start with “AQ.”, older ones with “AIza”.
gemini.step4: Paste it below. The free tier needs no payment method.

openai.step1: Sign in to the OpenAI platform and add a payment method. There is no free tier.
openai.step2: Under “API keys”, click “Create new secret key”.
openai.step3: Copy the key straight away. It starts with “sk-” and is shown only once.

anthropic.step1: Sign in to the Claude Console and add credit. There is no free tier.
anthropic.step3: Copy the key straight away. It starts with “sk-ant-” and is shown only once.

key.apiKeyHint: Stored encrypted in your browser and used only for requests to {{provider}}.
key.billingHint: A Google key looks the same whether or not billing is switched on. Applai cannot tell and therefore has to ask: as soon as a key is billed, a password is required.
key.billingPaid: Yes, billing is active for this project
key.passphraseWhyPaid: This key is billed. It is therefore encrypted with a password only you know. Without one, the material needed to decrypt it would sit next to the key in the browser.
key.passphraseFieldHint: At least {{min}} characters, not a single repeated character, not a slice of the API key.
key.passphraseWhyLength: At least {{min}} characters. The reason is concrete: anyone who copies the encrypted entry out of the browser can then try passwords at leisure, as fast as their graphics card allows. Nobody locks them out after ten failed attempts. A short password falls within hours, a long one takes years. Four random words in a row are easier to remember than a short string of special characters, and much harder to guess.
key.passphraseLimits: Applai only checks the length and two obviously worthless cases. It cannot judge whether your password is actually hard to guess.
key.passphraseNoReset: The password is stored nowhere and cannot be reset. If you forget it, you have to enter the API key again.

errors.controlCharacters: The API key contains line breaks or other control characters. Please paste it without line breaks.
errors.billingUnanswered: Please answer whether this key is billed.
errors.passphraseRequired: A password is required for a billed key.
errors.passphraseTooShort: The password must be at least {{min}} characters long.
errors.passphraseRepeated: The password consists of a single repeated character. Please use different characters.
errors.passphraseInKey: The password must not be part of the API key. Please choose a separate password.
errors.passphraseMismatch: The two passwords do not match.
errors.insecureOrigin: Applai needs a secure connection (HTTPS) to store the key encrypted. Over an unencrypted connection the browser does not provide the functions required for that.
errors.storage: The key could not be saved. Please try again.

corrupted.heading: The stored key could not be read
corrupted.body: Applai cannot tell which of these it is: the entry itself may be damaged, or the browser may simply not be releasing the storage right now, for example in private mode or while the app is open in a second tab. Reload the page first and close other tabs. If it stays that way, the only way on is to delete the stored key and enter it again afterwards.

paidHints.heading: If this key is billed
paidHints.intro: The key is stored encrypted in your browser. Even so: anyone who gets hold of it can make requests at your expense. These settings at the provider limit the damage.

limit.title: Set a spending limit
limit.gemini: A budget in the Google Cloud console only warns. It stops neither the usage nor the billing; it sends an email once a threshold is passed. Set it anyway so you notice early, but do not rely on it.
limit.openai: OpenAI distinguishes two things: a spend alert only sends a message and lets the requests carry on. Only the “Enforce a hard limit” setting answers further requests with an error once the monthly amount is reached.
limit.anthropic: In the Claude Console a monthly spending limit can be set per workspace. That is not possible for the default workspace, so create one of your own and generate the key inside it.

dedicated.title: A separate key used only for Applai
dedicated.body: Create a key you use nowhere else. Then you can see in the invoice what Applai accounts for, and you can revoke it on its own if you suspect anything, without interrupting your other applications.

scope.title: Allow the key for the Gemini API only
scope.body: The Google Cloud credentials let you decide which APIs a key may address at all. Restricted to the Gemini API, a key that goes astray cannot use any other billable Google service in the same project. Keys newly created in Google AI Studio are restricted like this by default; older keys and ones from the Cloud console are not.

unlock.heading: Unlock your key
unlock.intro: You protected the stored key with a passphrase. Without it Applai cannot read the key and cannot send anything to the provider.
unlock.wrong: The key could not be decrypted with this passphrase. Please check what you typed.
unlock.forgotten: The passphrase cannot be reset. If you have forgotten it, store a new key in the settings. Keep in mind that OpenAI and Anthropic show a key only once.

errors.invalid_key: The API key is invalid or has expired. Please check it in Settings.
errors.rate_limit: The provider is currently overloaded. Please try again shortly.
errors.quota: The API key's quota has been used up.
errors.quota_gemini: Gemini's free daily quota has been used up. It resets tomorrow, or you can add your own paid key.
errors.network: The request could not be sent. Please check your internet connection.
errors.blocked: The provider blocked the response for safety reasons.
errors.unknown: Unexpected error while calling the provider.

start.intro: Drop in your cover letter, paste the job ad, and move on to the workspace. Everything stays in this browser until you ask for a passage to be rewritten.
start.storageUnavailable: Your browser is not releasing its storage right now. You can keep working, but Applai will remember none of it: no draft, no settings, no application list. In private mode this is normal.

documents.heading: Your documents
documents.rule: Either one is enough. With both, the AI has more established facts to work from and has to leave less unsaid.

files.letterDescription: Word file (.docx) or PDF. The layout of a Word file survives the export untouched.
files.cvDescription: Word file (.docx) or PDF. Used as a basis of facts; editing it is not part of this build stage.
files.none: No file chosen yet. You can drag one here.
files.fromDraft: the document you last worked on

errors.unsupportedType: Applai reads Word files (.docx) and PDF files. Any other format cannot be opened.
errors.passwordProtected: This PDF file is password protected. Please remove the protection and choose it again.
errors.unreadable: The file could not be read. It may be damaged, or it may not be a Word or PDF document despite its extension.

pdf.beta: Read from a PDF. Converting it to Word is a beta feature: it restores paragraphs, headings and bullet points, but neither the original layout nor images or tables. Please read the result in the workspace before you use it.
pdf.multiColumn: This PDF is laid out in several columns. The conversion reads it line by line across the full page width, so text from the left and the right column ends up interleaved. For this document a Word file is by far the better source.

recent.heading: Last used
recent.body: This browser still holds a draft. You can carry on with it instead of looking for the file again. Drafts are deleted automatically after seven days.

name.label: Your name
name.hint: Applai replaces your name with a placeholder before every request. To do that it has to know what your name is. It will not guess.
name.detected: Taken from the top of your document. Please check it: what gets detected is the first name-shaped line, and that can be a company name.

jobAd.heading: Job ad
jobAd.label: Text of the ad
jobAd.hint: Paste the full text. The more of it is here, the more precise the list of requirements will be.
jobAd.pdfLabel: Or read it from a PDF file
jobAd.pdfHint: A link to the ad cannot be fetched: that would need a server to load the page for you, and Applai deliberately has none.

applications.heading: Application list
applications.empty: No application recorded yet. An entry appears once you export a finished cover letter.
applications.duplicate: This ad mentions a company you have already applied to: {{entries}}. That may be a coincidence: the check compares company names and nothing else.

missing.heading: Still missing:
missing.document: a cover letter or a CV
missing.jobAd: the text of the job ad

settings.storageUnavailable: Your browser is not releasing its storage right now. Changes made here apply to this session only.
settings.saveFailed: The change could not be saved and has been undone. Please try again.

appearance.heading: Appearance
appearance.hint: Light is the default. “Match the system” follows your operating system setting.
appearance.label: Display

language.heading: Interface language
language.hint: On first start Applai preselects your browser language. Your choice here applies from then on.
language.label: Language

anonymize.heading: Anonymisation
anonymize.label: Replace personal data before sending
anonymize.hint: Name, address, date of birth, phone number and email address are replaced with placeholders before any text goes to the provider, and swapped back in the answer.
anonymize.off: Without anonymisation your personal data goes to the chosen provider in the clear.

truthMode.heading: Truth boundary
truthMode.hint: How far may a phrasing move away from what your documents actually establish?
truthMode.label: Boundary

explanations.strict: Only what is in your documents gets rephrased. A required skill that is missing stays in the gap list instead of appearing in the text.
explanations.bridge: Generalisations that your own statements cover are allowed as well, such as “experience with relational databases” where your CV says PostgreSQL. No new facts come into being.
explanations.free: The AI may add what is not established. Such passages are marked in colour and have to be confirmed one by one; while any of them is unconfirmed, the export stays locked.

key.heading: Provider and API key
key.currentProvider: A key for {{provider}} is stored. The provider changes together with the key; you replace both below.

backup.heading: Backup
backup.hint: Save the application list, drafts and settings as a file, and restore them on another device or after a deletion. The API key is not part of it. It stays in the browser where you entered it.
backup.importWarning: Restoring replaces everything you have; nothing is merged.

errors.export: The backup could not be created. Please try again.
errors.import: The file could not be restored. It is damaged, not an Applai backup, or from a newer version. What you had is unchanged.

delete.heading: Delete all data
delete.body: Removes the application list, drafts, settings and the stored API key from this device. Nothing of Applai is left afterwards. Your key at the provider stays alive. Revoke it there when you no longer need it.
delete.confirmBody: The application list, drafts, settings and the stored API key will be removed. This cannot be undone; only a backup downloaded beforehand brings the list back.
delete.done: Everything has been deleted: application list, drafts, settings and the API key.
delete.storageFailed: The API key was deleted, but the application list, drafts and settings were not. Please reload the page and try again.
delete.vaultFailed: The application list, drafts and settings were deleted, but the stored API key was not. Please reload the page and try again.
delete.bothFailed: Nothing was deleted. Your browser is not releasing its storage right now. Please close other tabs with Applai, reload the page and try again.
